newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak up on Remgro takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Malbak up on Remgro takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in recently-unbundled South African firm Malbak Ltd rose over two percent in modest trade on Monday, buoyed by talk that conglomerate Rembrandt (Remgro) was set to buy a stake in it, dealers said.
They said Malbak, now focused in the packaging sector since its restructure, also looked to be on the road to posting strong results.
"All of the demand is on the restructuring. The talk of the Rembrandt interest is part of that," said a share dealer.
At 1300 GMT, Malbak, which completed a rigorous unbundling of its diverse industrial interests last month, was up 16 cents to 670 cents in volume of over 374,000 shares.
South Africa's Business Times newspaper reported on Sunday that it was "common knowledge in the market" that Remgro was keen to buy Malbak and merge their packaging interests.
Neither Remgro nor Malbak were immediately available for comment.

Remgro's packaging operations are held largely through a 30 percent stake in Printpak and a 17 percent stake in Lenco, the paper said. Malbak's primary assets since the unbundling are a 68 percent stake in Kohler Ltd and a 64 percent interest in U.K-listed MY Holdings Plc
However, not all analysts were convinced of the takeover rumours.
"It was known before the unbundling that Remgro was interested in Malbak's food interests, not packaging. Also Lenco is really a tiny part of Remgro," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"Remgro has a lot on its plate sorting out its other interests before it is likely to think of taking over Malbak."
Traders said Malbak had seen a seen a fair amount of institutional interest in the past couple of weeks.
The rise in its share price on Monday was also seen on bargain-hunting after the stock fell as low as 646 cents last week.

Malbak said in May that a satisfactory set of results was expected for the year to end-August. It said that pro-forma attributable earnings for the six months to end-February would have shown a 25 percent rise to 71 million rand.
Remgro shares were also up two percent or 90 cents to 45.90 rand.
